title: BatchCache Guardian: Response playbook and human-gated apply strategy for cost-tuner incidents
creator: Ava Martinez
description: After two recent incidents where the automatic batching/caching advisor applied aggressive configuration changes that produced increased latency for tail requests and out-of-spec regressions for a set of paid customers, we need a compact, operator-friendly playbook that combines automated recommendations with human-in-the-loop validation. This ticket creates the BatchCache Guardian playbook: a step-by-step response and safe-apply workflow that integrates checklists, telemetry gates, shadow-simulations, and fast rollback controls.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented playbook committed to the Optimize runbooks Confluence page. 2) A validated CI harness that can run a shadow-sim of a candidate batching/caching policy against representative traces. 3) An operator-facing apply UI flow prototype that enforces gating checks (canary percentage, cost delta, latency SLO checks) before commit. 4) A tested rollback button that executes in <60s and reverts kernel-affecting runtime flags. 5) Runbook reviewed and signed off by Reliability and Product Security.
steps: Draft initial playbook with explicit stages: Analyze -> Simulate -> Canary -> Promote -> Monitor -> Rollback
Wire the playbook to the Optimize suggestion engine to produce a candidate bundle (config + rationale + expected savings + risk tags)
Build a shadow-simulation job that replays live traces at sampled QPS to the candidate config in isolated runtime (no external traffic impact)
Add telemetry gates: token-latency-p50/p95/p99, error-rate, NLP-quality-eval pass/fail on a canned prompt set, median-cost-per-token
Prototype operator UI with mandatory checklist and automated gate status; add an emergency rollback button and audit log link
Create an automated canary promotion policy: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with time windows and automated abort on gate failures
Document manual rollback procedure for kernel/driver-level flags and GPU pool reconfiguration
Schedule tabletop run and a smoke test window to validate the whole flow
investigation_notes: Root cause from prior incidents: the auto-apply path lacked workload shadowing and relied on historical averages; distributional shift in sequence length exposed poor kernel selection for some model variants. Observability gaps: missing per-route evals and insufficient context for prompted regressions. Cost signal was prioritized without a conservative latency guard. We analyzed traces from 2025-01-28 to 2025-02-11 and identified a cohort of heavy-tail requests that drive p99 latency increases when batching/chunking heuristics are too aggressive.
mitigation_plan: Short-term: revert the last applied aggressor configs and enable a temporary circuit-breaker to prevent auto-apply for routes with p99 > configured threshold. Medium-term: implement shadow-simulations and gating in the Optimize control plane. Long-term: enhance advisory ML model to include p99 sensitivity and create a risk score for each recommendation.
rollback_procedure: 1) Operator triggers 'Immediate rollback' from the Console which kicks an orchestration job to restore previous config bundle across all instances. 2) If the orchestration job fails, run the manual kernel-flag revert script on affected GPU nodes (link to runbook snippet). 3) Escalate to on-call infra PO and open a hotfix PR to pin the advisor to conservative defaults. 4) Notify customers per incident comms template and create a follow-up postmortem.
followups: Add per-route eval suite to the CI that runs on each advisor suggested change
Expose an API for customers to opt-out of auto-applies per route (product request)
Create a telemetry dashboard tile that surfaces risk-score, gating status, and recent rollbacks
Instrument synthetic user journeys for the heavy-tail prompts identified in investigation_notes
